disease_label_per_paper: Catastrophic systemic reaction and fatal (fulminant) disseminated intravascular coagulation following high-pressure intrapelvic povidone-iodine instillation during augmentation cystoplasty
presentation_summary: 52-year-old woman with genitourinary tuberculosis on four-drug antitubercular therapy (3 months), solitary functioning right kidney with percutaneous nephrostomy, undergoing augmentation cystoplasty with right ureteric reimplantation; preoperative Hb 12 g/dL, TLC 5.6 x10^9/L, platelets 156 x10^9/L, creatinine 1.2 mg/dL, INR 0.91; perioperative piperacillin-tazobactam.

Dilute povidone-iodine was instilled antegradely through the nephrostomy under pressure; within 5-10 minutes she developed rigors, then progressive diffuse oozing from raw operative surfaces and progressive hypotension requiring vasopressors and 2 units PRBC.

Initial postoperative labs: Hb 6.6 g/dL, platelets 91 x10^9/L, INR 2.46, aPTT 60.6 s, creatinine 1.57 mg/dL; generalized abdominal distension, persistent diffuse wound and drain-site bleeding, extensive ecchymoses; ultrasound without significant intra-abdominal collection.

baseline_preoperative_record.finding: Earlier history: azotemia with creatinine 2.1 mg/dL before nephrostomy, normalized after PCN
baseline_preoperative_record.source_text_value: presented with azotemia and a serum creatinine of 2.1 mg/dL ... A right percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) was performed, resulting in normalization of renal function.

clinical_course_record.finding: Re-exploration within 12 hours: diffuse intra-abdominal oozing without discrete bleeding source; intraoperative PT 38.3 s, INR 3.23, aPTT >120 s; damage-control packing; death 2 h later
clinical_course_record.source_text_value: Intraoperative coagulation studies demonstrated marked worsening of the coagulopathy, with a prothrombin time of 38.3 seconds, an INR of 3.23, and an activated partial thromboplastin time exceeding 120 seconds. ... The patient died 2 h after re-exploration.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Paper's diagnostic adjudication: clinical course characteristic of fulminant DIC; fibrinogen, D-dimer, serum iodine, blood cultures and autopsy not obtained
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The subsequent clinical course was characteristic of fulminant DIC. ... The absence of serum iodine measurements, fibrinogen, D-dimer, blood cultures, and a postmortem examination represents an important limitation

actual_treatment: massive transfusion (packed red blood cells, fresh frozen plasma, platelet concentrates)
emergency re-exploration with damage-control abdominal packing

outcome.source_text_value: The patient died 2 h after re-exploration.

quality_warnings: Presentation is an intraoperative/early postoperative event (day 0); no numeric vital signs are reported. Quantitative presentation evidence is 5 initial postoperative labs.

Fibrinogen and D-dimer were not measured; DIC is a clinical diagnosis by the authors. Blood cultures were not obtained, so infection/endotoxemia as trigger is unresolved (paper does not diagnose sepsis).
Hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL was measured after 2 units PRBC were given intraoperatively.
Preoperative baseline labs and re-exploration labs are recorded but non-ranking.
